title: Pieter Levels on remote work, bootstrapping, and finding meaning as a nomad
summary: Pieter Levels talks with SafetyWing's Sondre about how remote work is going mainstream, why he stays bootstrapped, and why meaning comes from people rather than aesthetics. He explains how Nomad List started as a fix for his own problem and which problems remote workers still need solved.

principles.text: Build products by solving your own problem; Nomad List began as his own need to find the next city.
principles.quote: It was more of a solving my own problem because back then I was nomading a lot more rapidly than now

principles.text: Bootstrapping keeps you wired to the market: revenue shows instantly whether a change works.
principles.quote: because it's bootstrapped, you're so tapped into the market as a signal where anything you do to your startup or website, you immediately see if it works or not because you make money on it or not.

principles.text: VC money blurs market feedback and removes the incentive to build revenue; odds of an exit are low without an unfair advantage.
principles.quote: And with venture capital, you have all this money in your bank account, you know, you can spend it on all these things and there's not a lot of incentive, especially in the beginning, to, you know, build revenue or profit.

principles.text: Fringe ideas can become mainstream; early pushback reflects culture, not arguments, so keep pushing, then look for the next fringe.
principles.quote: every fringe subculture has potential to become mainstream because usually you're an early adopter that's to something that will absolutely not be accepted in the beginning by mainstream society.

principles.text: Half-remote companies break culturally; be fully in-office or fully remote.
principles.quote: it's very difficult to have companies that are half remote where like some people from the team work remotely and some people stay in the office.

principles.text: Improve existing places and communities rather than trying to build new villages from scratch.
principles.quote: instead of trying to create new villages, which reinvent the whole concept of society, try to iterate on the society you're currently living in.
